// STEP 0: GLOBAL CONFIGURATION
// Electro-Acoustic Ensemble Companion
// ==========================================
(
~splits = (
    bassMax: 45, // A2
    padMax: 72,  // C5
    bellMax: 96  // C7
);

~cc = (
    // Mixer
    vol1: 81, vol2: 82, vol3: 83, vol4: 84,
    // Timbre & Mod
    bassFilt: 71, padMorph: 72, bellFm: 73, airSweep: 74,
    // Global FX
    delayTime: 75, delayFb: 76, verbDecay: 77, verbMix: 78
);
)


// ==========================================
// STEP 1: DISCOVERY
// ==========================================
MIDIClient.init;


// ==========================================
// STEP 2: CONNECTION
// ==========================================
(
var inDeviceName = "Your MIDI Device Name Here"; // <-- USER: PASTE DEVICE NAME HERE

~myInDevice = MIDIClient.sources.detect { |src| src.device == inDeviceName };

if(~myInDevice.notNil) {
    MIDIIn.connect(0, ~myInDevice);
    "MIDI IN connected successfully to: ".post; ~myInDevice.device.postln;
    ~myUid = ~myInDevice.uid;
} {
    "Warning: MIDI IN device not found! Please update 'inDeviceName' and re-run.".warn;
    ~myUid = nil;
};
)


// ==========================================
// STEP 3: AUDIO SERVER, ROUTING & SYNTHESIS
// ==========================================
(
s.options.memSize = 65536;
s.boot;

s.waitForBoot({

    // A. BUFFERS (Wavetables for Zone 2 Pad)
    ~wt_morph = Buffer.allocConsecutive(4, s, 2048, 1);
    s.sync;
    
    ~wt_morph[0].loadCollection(Signal.sineFill(1024, [1]).asWavetable);
    ~wt_morph[1].loadCollection(Signal.sineFill(1024, [1, 0.5, 0.25]).asWavetable);
    ~wt_morph[2].loadCollection(Signal.sineFill(1024, 1/(1..10)).asWavetable);
    ~wt_morph[3].loadCollection(Signal.sineFill(1024, Array.fill(10, { 1.0.rand })).asWavetable);
    s.sync;

    // B. CONTROL BUSES & STATE DICTIONARY
    ~ccVals = (
        vol1: 0.8, vol2: 0.7, vol3: 0.7, vol4: 0.6,
        bassFilt: 0.5, padMorph: 0.5, bellFm: 0.5, airSweep: 0.5,
        delayTime: 0.4, delayFb: 0.4, verbDecay: 0.6, verbMix: 0.3
    );

    ~buses = ();
    ~ccVals.keysValuesDo { |key, val| ~buses[key] = Bus.control(s, 1).set(val) };

    // C. AUDIO ROUTING
    ~synthGroup = Group.new(s);
    ~fxGroup = Group.after(~synthGroup);
    ~masterGroup = Group.after(~fxGroup);

    ~groupBus = Bus.audio(s, 2);
    ~verbBus = Bus.audio(s, 2);
    ~masterBus = Bus.audio(s, 2);

    // D. SYNTHDEFS

    // --- EFFECTS ---
    
    // Tier 2: Tape Delay
    SynthDef(\fx_TapeDelay, { |in, out, timeBus, fbBus|
        var sig = In.ar(in, 2);
        var time = Lag.kr(In.kr(timeBus).linexp(0, 1, 0.05, 1.0), 0.1);
        var fb = In.kr(fbBus).linlin(0, 1, 0.1, 0.85);
        var delay = CombL.ar(sig, 2.0, time, time * fb * 10);
        delay = LPF.ar(delay, 2500); // Dark, degrading repeats
        Out.ar(out, sig + (delay * 0.6));
    }).add;

    // Tier 2: Ensemble Reverb
    SynthDef(\fx_EnsembleVerb, { |in, out, mixBus, decayBus|
        var sig = In.ar(in, 2);
        var mix = In.kr(mixBus);
        var decay = In.kr(decayBus).linlin(0, 1, 0.1, 0.95);
        var verb = FreeVerb2.ar(sig[0], sig[1], mix, decay, 0.2);
        Out.ar(out, verb);
    }).add;

    // Tier 3: Master EQ & Limiter
    SynthDef(\fx_Master, { |in, out=0|
        var sig = In.ar(in, 2);
        // Carve out mid-range for Saxophone & Guitar (1.5kHz, -6dB)
        sig = BPeakEQ.ar(sig, 1500, 1.0, -6.0);
        sig = Limiter.ar(sig, 0.95, 0.01);
        Out.ar(out, sig);
    }).add;

    // --- GENERATORS ---

    // Zone 1: Subterranean Anchor (Mono, Subtractive, Velocity -> Filter Env)
    SynthDef(\zone1_Bass, { arg out=0, freq=65.41, gate=1, vel=0.8, filtBus, zoneVol=1.0;
        var lagFreq = Lag.kr(freq, 0.1); // Portamento
        var env = EnvGen.kr(Env.asr(0.02, 1.0, 0.1), gate, doneAction: 2);
        var sig = Saw.ar(lagFreq) + Pulse.ar(lagFreq * 0.99, 0.5);
        
        var baseCutoff = In.kr(filtBus).linexp(0, 1, 80, 4000);
        var filtEnv = EnvGen.kr(Env.adsr(0.02, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1), gate);
        var filtDepth = vel.pow(2).linexp(0.0, 1.0, 100, 6000); // Exponential velocity response
        
        sig = RLPF.ar(sig, (baseCutoff + (filtEnv * filtDepth)).clip(20, 18000), 0.3);
        sig = (sig * 1.5).tanh; // Local wavefolding/saturation
        
        Out.ar(out, Pan2.ar(sig * env * zoneVol * 0.5, 0)); // Bypasses Group FX, straight to Master
    }).add;

    // Zone 2: Harmonic Glue Pad (Poly, Wavetable, Velocity Ignored)
    SynthDef(\zone2_Pad, { arg out=0, freq=261.6, gate=1, morphBus, bufBase, zoneVol=1.0;
        var env = EnvGen.kr(Env.asr(1.5, 1.0, 2.5), gate, doneAction: 2);
        var morphSpeed = In.kr(morphBus).linlin(0, 1, 0.1, 5.0);
        
        var index = LFNoise2.kr(morphSpeed).range(0, 3);
        var sig = VOsc.ar(bufBase + index, freq * [0.995, 1.005]); // Stereo detune
        
        var pan = LFNoise2.kr(0.2).range(-0.6, 0.6); // Shifting stereo image
        sig = sig + DelayC.ar(sig, 0.05, SinOsc.kr(0.3).range(0.015, 0.025), 0.5); // Local Chorus
        
        Out.ar(out, Balance2.ar(sig[0], sig[1], pan, env * zoneVol * 0.35));
    }).add;

    // Zone 3: Kinetic Glass Bells (Poly, FM, Velocity -> Index & Amp)
    SynthDef(\zone3_Bells, { arg out=0, freq=1046.5, vel=0.8, fmBus, zoneVol=1.0;
        var env = EnvGen.kr(Env.perc(0.005, 1.2), doneAction: 2); // No sustain
        
        var fmBase = In.kr(fmBus).linexp(0, 1, 0.1, 15.0);
        var fmIndex = vel.pow(2) * fmBase * 1000; // Exponential velocity -> chaos
        
        var mod = SinOsc.ar(freq * 3.5) * fmIndex * env;
        var sig = SinOsc.ar(freq + mod);
        
        sig = Splay.ar(sig ! 2); // Local stereo spread
        Out.ar(out, sig * env * vel * zoneVol * 0.25);
    }).add;

    // Zone 4: Stratospheric Air (Poly, BPF Noise, Breathing Envelope)
    SynthDef(\zone4_Air, { arg out=0, freq=2093, gate=1, vel=0.8, sweepBus, zoneVol=1.0;
        var env = EnvGen.kr(Env.asr(2.0, 1.0, 3.0), gate, doneAction: 2);
        var sweepRate = In.kr(sweepBus).linexp(0, 1, 0.05, 2.0);
        
        var sweep = SinOsc.kr(sweepRate).exprange(freq * 0.5, freq * 2.0).clip(200, 18000);
        var sig = WhiteNoise.ar(0.5) + PinkNoise.ar(0.5);
        
        sig = Resonz.ar(sig, sweep, 0.1) * 15.0; // Compensate for narrow bandwidth
        sig = HPF.ar(sig, 4000); // Local HPF: Zero low-mid mud
        
        Out.ar(out, Pan2.ar(sig * env * vel * zoneVol * 0.4, 0));
    }).add;

    s.sync;

    // E. INSTANTIATE EFFECTS
    ~tapeDelay = Synth(\fx_TapeDelay, [
        \in, ~groupBus, \out, ~verbBus,
        \timeBus, ~buses.delayTime, \fbBus, ~buses.delayFb
    ], target: ~fxGroup, addAction: \addToTail);

    ~hallVerb = Synth(\fx_EnsembleVerb, [
        \in, ~verbBus, \out, ~masterBus,
        \mixBus, ~buses.verbMix, \decayBus, ~buses.verbDecay
    ], target: ~fxGroup, addAction: \addToTail);

    ~masterLimiter = Synth(\fx_Master, [
        \in, ~masterBus, \out, 0
    ], target: ~masterGroup, addAction: \addToTail);

    // F. SYNTH STATE & MIDI
    ~notes = Array.newClear(128);
    ~monoBassSynth = nil;
    ~monoBassNote = nil;

    MIDIdef.cc(\ensembleCC, { |val, num|
        var mapped = val / 127.0;
        case
            { num == ~cc.vol1 } { ~buses.vol1.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\vol1] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.vol2 } { ~buses.vol2.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\vol2] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.vol3 } { ~buses.vol3.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\vol3] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.vol4 } { ~buses.vol4.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\vol4] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.bassFilt } { ~buses.bassFilt.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\bassFilt] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.padMorph } { ~buses.padMorph.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\padMorph] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.bellFm } { ~buses.bellFm.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\bellFm] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.airSweep } { ~buses.airSweep.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\airSweep] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.delayTime } { ~buses.delayTime.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\delayTime] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.delayFb } { ~buses.delayFb.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\delayFb] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.verbDecay } { ~buses.verbDecay.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\verbDecay] = mapped; }
            { num == ~cc.verbMix } { ~buses.verbMix.set(mapped); ~ccVals[\verbMix] = mapped; };
    }, srcID: ~myUid);

    MIDIdef.noteOn(\ensembleOn, { |velocity, noteNum, channel, src|
        var freq = noteNum.midicps;
        var vel = velocity / 127.0;

        if(noteNum <= ~splits.bassMax) {
            // Zone 1: Mono Bass
            if(~monoBassSynth.isNil) {
                ~monoBassSynth = Synth(\zone1_Bass, [
                    \out, ~masterBus, \freq, freq, \vel, vel, \gate, 1,
                    \filtBus, ~buses.bassFilt, \zoneVol, ~buses.vol1.asMap
                ], target: ~synthGroup);
            } {
                ~monoBassSynth.set(\freq, freq, \vel, vel);
            };
            ~monoBassNote = noteNum;
        } {
            // Polyphonic Zones
            if(~notes[noteNum].notNil) { ~notes[noteNum].set(\gate, 0); };

            ~notes[noteNum] = case
                { noteNum <= ~splits.padMax } {
                    Synth(\zone2_Pad, [
                        \out, ~groupBus, \freq, freq, \gate, 1,
                        \morphBus, ~buses.padMorph, \bufBase, ~wt_morph[0].bufnum, \zoneVol, ~buses.vol2.asMap
                    ], target: ~synthGroup);
                }
                { noteNum <= ~splits.bellMax } {
                    Synth(\zone3_Bells, [
                        \out, ~groupBus, \freq, freq, \vel, vel,
                        \fmBus, ~buses.bellFm, \zoneVol, ~buses.vol3.asMap
                    ], target: ~synthGroup);
                }
                { noteNum > ~splits.bellMax } {
                    Synth(\zone4_Air, [
                        \out, ~groupBus, \freq, freq, \gate, 1, \vel, vel,
                        \sweepBus, ~buses.airSweep, \zoneVol, ~buses.vol4.asMap
                    ], target: ~synthGroup);
                };
        };
    }, srcID: ~myUid);

    MIDIdef.noteOff(\ensembleOff, { |velocity, noteNum, channel, src|
        if(noteNum <= ~splits.bassMax) {
            if(noteNum == ~monoBassNote) {
                if(~monoBassSynth.notNil) {
                    ~monoBassSynth.set(\gate, 0);
                    ~monoBassSynth = nil;
                    ~monoBassNote = nil;
                };
            };
        } {
            if(~notes[noteNum].notNil) {
                ~notes[noteNum].set(\gate, 0);
                ~notes[noteNum] = nil;
            };
        };
    }, srcID: ~myUid);

    "Electro-Acoustic Ensemble Synth Initialized.".postln;
});
)

// STEP 4: ADVANCED UI

(
defer {
    if(~ensWin.notNil and: { ~ensWin.isClosed.not }) { ~ensWin.close };

    ~ensWin = Window("Ensemble Companion", Rect(100, 100, 640, 520));
    ~ensWin.view.decorator = FlowLayout(~ensWin.view.bounds, 15@15, 10@15);
    ~ensWin.view.background = Color.fromHexString("#1E2124");

    // --- VERTICAL MIXER (Left Side) ---
    ~mixerView = CompositeView(~ensWin, 250@300);
    ~mixerView.decorator = FlowLayout(~mixerView.bounds, 5@5, 15@0);

    StaticText(~mixerView, 240@25).string_("ZONE MIXER").stringColor_(Color.cyan).font_(Font("Arial", 14, true)).align_(\center);

    ~slVol1 = EZSlider(~mixerView, 45@250, "Bass", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.vol1.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\vol1] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\vol1], layout: \vert)
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~slVol2 = EZSlider(~mixerView, 45@250, "Pad", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.vol2.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\vol2] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\vol2], layout: \vert)
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~slVol3 = EZSlider(~mixerView, 45@250, "Bells", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.vol3.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\vol3] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\vol3], layout: \vert)
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~slVol4 = EZSlider(~mixerView, 45@250, "Air", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.vol4.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\vol4] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\vol4], layout: \vert)
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);

    // --- TIMBRE & MOD KNOBS (Right Side) ---
    ~modView = CompositeView(~ensWin, 340@300);
    ~modView.decorator = FlowLayout(~modView.bounds, 10@5, 20@20);

    StaticText(~modView, 320@25).string_("TIMBRE & MODULATION").stringColor_(Color.cyan).font_(Font("Arial", 14, true)).align_(\center);

    ~knBassFilt = EZKnob(~modView, 80@100, "Bass Cut", \amp, { |kn| ~buses.bassFilt.set(kn.value); ~ccVals[\bassFilt] = kn.value; }, ~ccVals[\bassFilt])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~knPadMorph = EZKnob(~modView, 80@100, "Pad Spd", \amp, { |kn| ~buses.padMorph.set(kn.value); ~ccVals[\padMorph] = kn.value; }, ~ccVals[\padMorph])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~knBellFm = EZKnob(~modView, 80@100, "Bell FM", \amp, { |kn| ~buses.bellFm.set(kn.value); ~ccVals[\bellFm] = kn.value; }, ~ccVals[\bellFm])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.yellow);
    ~knAirSweep = EZKnob(~modView, 80@100, "Air Rate", \amp, { |kn| ~buses.airSweep.set(kn.value); ~ccVals[\airSweep] = kn.value; }, ~ccVals[\airSweep])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.yellow);

    // --- GLOBAL FX (Bottom) ---
    ~fxView = CompositeView(~ensWin, 610@150);
    ~fxView.decorator = FlowLayout(~fxView.bounds, 5@5, 5@10);

    StaticText(~fxView, 600@25).string_("GLOBAL GROUP EFFECTS").stringColor_(Color.cyan).font_(Font("Arial", 14, true));

    ~slDelayTime = EZSlider(~fxView, 290@25, "Tape Time", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.delayTime.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\delayTime] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\delayTime])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~slVerbMix = EZSlider(~fxView, 290@25, "Verb Mix", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.verbMix.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\verbMix] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\verbMix])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~slDelayFb = EZSlider(~fxView, 290@25, "Tape Fdbk", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.delayFb.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\delayFb] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\delayFb])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);
    ~slVerbDec = EZSlider(~fxView, 290@25, "Verb Decay", \amp, { |sl| ~buses.verbDecay.set(sl.value); ~ccVals[\verbDecay] = sl.value; }, ~ccVals[\verbDecay])
        .setColors(stringColor: Color.white);

    ~ensWin.front;

    // GUI Polling Loop (AppClock)
    ~guiRoutine = Routine({
        loop {
            if(~slVol1.notNil) { ~slVol1.value = ~ccVals[\vol1] };
            if(~slVol2.notNil) { ~slVol2.value = ~ccVals[\vol2] };
            if(~slVol3.notNil) { ~slVol3.value = ~ccVals[\vol3] };
            if(~slVol4.notNil) { ~slVol4.value = ~ccVals[\vol4] };
            
            if(~knBassFilt.notNil) { ~knBassFilt.value = ~ccVals[\bassFilt] };
            if(~knPadMorph.notNil) { ~knPadMorph.value = ~ccVals[\padMorph] };
            if(~knBellFm.notNil) { ~knBellFm.value = ~ccVals[\bellFm] };
            if(~knAirSweep.notNil) { ~knAirSweep.value = ~ccVals[\airSweep] };
            
            if(~slDelayTime.notNil) { ~slDelayTime.value = ~ccVals[\delayTime] };
            if(~slDelayFb.notNil) { ~slDelayFb.value = ~ccVals[\delayFb] };
            if(~slVerbMix.notNil) { ~slVerbMix.value = ~ccVals[\verbMix] };
            if(~slVerbDec.notNil) { ~slVerbDec.value = ~ccVals[\verbDecay] };
            
            0.05.wait; // 20fps
        }
    }).play(AppClock);

    ~ensWin.onClose = {
        ~guiRoutine.stop;
        ~ensWin = nil;
        "GUI Closed.".postln;
    };
};
)


// ==========================================
// STEP 5: CLEANUP
// ==========================================
(
if(~ensWin.notNil and: { ~ensWin.isClosed.not }) { ~ensWin.close };
if(~guiRoutine.notNil) { ~guiRoutine.stop };

MIDIdef.freeAll;

if(~notes.notNil) {
    ~notes.do({ |synth| if(synth.notNil) { synth.set(\gate, 0); } });
    ~notes = nil;
};

if(~monoBassSynth.notNil) {
    ~monoBassSynth.set(\gate, 0);
    ~monoBassSynth = nil;
    ~monoBassNote = nil;
};

~tapeDelay.free;
~hallVerb.free;
~masterLimiter.free;

~buses.keysValuesDo { |key, bus| bus.free };

~groupBus.free;
~verbBus.free;
~masterBus.free;

~synthGroup.free;
~fxGroup.free;
~masterGroup.free;

if(~wt_morph.notNil) { ~wt_morph.do(_.free) };

"Ensemble Companion cleanup complete.".postln;
)

# SuperCollider Live Coding System Prompt

You are an expert SuperCollider (sclang) programmer specializing in continuous Ndef + Pbindef live coding using the JITLib framework. You generate complete, high-performance, structurally rigid code blocks for real-time algorithmic music.

## Output Rules
- Output ONLY valid SuperCollider code. No markdown prose, no explanations, no "Here is your code."
- Assume `t = TempoClock.default; t.tempo = 60/60; Pdef.defaultQuant = 1;` has already been run by the user. Do not include global tempo setup unless asked.
- Every section must be clearly labeled using the exact comment headers shown in the structural template.

## Architecture & Constraints
- **NO SynthDef/Synth**: All synthesis must be defined dynamically inside `Ndef` blocks.
- **Continuous Nodes**: Never use `doneAction: 2`. `Ndef`s must remain "alive" (running) to receive pattern data.
- **Trigger Management**: ALWAYS use `t_trig=1` (Control Rate Trigger) in the `Ndef` args and `\t_trig, 1` in the `Pbindef` to re-trigger envelopes.
- **Maximize Arguments**: Expose as many parameters as possible as `args` (e.g., `freq, amp, rq, modIndex, delayTime, rate`). Only use `var` for audio signal routing.
- **Stereo Imaging**: All audio `Ndef`s must be stereo (`Pan2.ar`, `Splay.ar`, or `!2`).
- **Dynamic UGens**: Use `DynKlank` instead of `Klank` so arrays update in real-time.
- **Mixing & Amplitude**: Be strictly mindful of instrument volume levels (`amp`). Balance the mix so multiple signals can coexist in the same sound space without clipping, overpowering each other, or creating muddy textures. Use `amp` scaling sensibly.

## 🚨 Acoustic Logic & Sound Design Anti-Patterns (CRITICAL) 🚨
- **The Lethal Finite Pattern Trap (CRITICAL)**: A pattern that ends outputs `nil`, permanently killing the `Pbindef` and silencing the instrument. Any subsequent effect tweaks will be applied to dead silence! You MUST wrap all finite generators (`Pgeom`, `Pseries`, finite `Pseq`/`Pwalk`) in an infinite loop: `Pn(Pgeom(0.125, 1.1, 8), inf)`. 
- **The Envelope/Trigger Trap**: NEVER use `Env.asr` or `Env.adsr` with `t_trig`. They will instantly click/mute. ALWAYS use fixed-duration envelopes like `Env.perc` or `Env([0, 1, 1, 0], [atk, sus, rel])`.
- **The Sine Wave Filter Trap**: NEVER use subtractive filters (`RLPF`, `LPF`, `BPF`) on a pure `SinOsc`. Sine waves have no harmonics to filter. Use FM Synthesis, waveshaping, or harmonically rich oscillators (`Saw`, `Pulse`) if filtering is required.
- **The GVerb Phasing Trap**: `GVerb.ar` expects a MONO input. If your `Ndef` signal is stereo, you MUST sum it: `GVerb.ar(in.sum, ...)`.
- **The Wet/Dry Reverb Trap**: When putting `FreeVerb` or `GVerb` in a filter slot, its internal mix MUST be set to 1 (100% wet). JITLib's `\wet10` handles the actual crossfade. (e.g., `FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.8, 0.5)`).
- **The Dead Delay Trap**: Do not use `DelayN` or `DelayC` for echoes. Use `CombL` or `CombC` so there is feedback.

## The Routing Standard
- **Slot [0]**: Audio source. Declared via `Ndef(\name, { ... }).play;`.
- **NO Destructive Chaining (CRITICAL)**: NEVER use the `<<>` operator (e.g., `Ndef(\master) <<> Ndef(\name)`). It overwrites previous inputs and destroys the mix. Rely purely on `.play` to send audio to the main outputs.
- **Slot [1]**: Control Pattern. Declared via `Ndef(\name)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\seqName);`.
- **Slots [10, 11, 12]**: Effects (Reverb, Delay, Distortion/Filter). Declared via `Ndef(\name)[10] = \filter -> { |in| ... };`. Always initialize their wetness to 0: `Ndef(\name).set(\wet10, 0);`.

## Live Coding Tweak Rules
- **Crossfading Tweaks (CRITICAL)**: Prefer `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` over `.set` whenever possible to facilitate smooth crossfading of changes. Ensure the Ndef has a `fadeTime` defined to control the transition speed.
- **Instrument Tweaks**: Use `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` ONLY for parameters NOT controlled by the `Pbindef`.
- **Sequence Tweaks**: Use `Pbindef(\seqName, \param, value)` for ANY parameter actively sequenced.
- **Comments**: Every tweak MUST have a descriptive inline comment explaining its sonic result.
- **Reversion Comments**: Every tweak you output MUST be immediately followed by a commented line showing the exact code needed to revert the parameter(s) back to their prior state before this tweak. (e.g., `// Ndef(\name).xset(\param, old_value); // Revert to previous state`).

## Structural Template & Example

// --- [NAME] INSTRUMENTS ---
(
Ndef(\toad).clear;
Ndef(\toad, {
	|freq=150, modFreq=50, res=0.1, amp=0.8, t_trig=1|
	var env, mod, sig;
	env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.2), t_trig);
	mod = SinOsc.ar(modFreq) * freq;
	sig = Saw.ar(freq + mod);
	sig = RLPF.ar(sig, freq * 2, res);
	Pan2.ar(sig * env * amp, 0);
}).play;
)

// --- [NAME] EFFECTS ---
(
// reverb (Index 10)
Ndef(\toad)[10] = \filter -> { |in| FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.7, 0.2) };
Ndef(\toad).set(\wet10, 0);

// delay (Index 11)
Ndef(\toad)[11] = \filter -> { |in| CombL.ar(in, 0.2, 0.1, 1.5) };
Ndef(\toad).set(\wet11, 0);

// distortion (Index 12)
Ndef(\toad)[12] = \filter -> { |in| (in * 5).fold2(0.8) };
Ndef(\toad).set(\wet12, 0);
)

// --- [NAME] SEQUENCES ---
(
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.5, \freq, Pwhite(100, 200), \t_trig, 1);
Ndef(\toad).quant = 1;
Ndef(\toad)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\toadSeq);
)

// --- [NAME] LIVE CODING TWEAKS ---

//instrument tweaks
Ndef(\toad).fadeTime = 2; // Set fade time for smooth crossfades
Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.5); // Thin, watery resonance
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.1); // Revert to initial resonance
Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.05, \modFreq, 200); // Aggressive FM croak
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.5, \modFreq, 50); // Revert to previous watery resonance

//sequence tweaks
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.125, \freq, 300); // Fast, high-pitched defensive chatter
// Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.5, \freq, Pwhite(100, 200)); // Revert to base sequence
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, Pwrand([0.25, 0.5, 1], [0.6, 0.3, 0.1], inf)); // Uneven, hesitant hopping rhythm
// Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.125); // Revert rhythmic duration
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \freq, Pn(Pgeom(100, 1.1, 8), inf)); // Repeating upward pitch sweep
// Pbindef(\toadSeq, \freq, Pwhite(100, 200)); // Revert sequence freq

//effect tweaks
Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet11, 0.6); // Add rhythmic slapback delay
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet11, 0); // Revert delay mix
Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet10, 0.8, \wet12, 1.0); // Massive distorted cave echo
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet10, 0, \wet12, 0); // Revert reverb and distortion
Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet10, 0, \wet11, 0, \wet12, 0); // Return to dry signal

//[name] fade out and ending
(
Pbindef(\toadSeq).stop;
Ndef(\toad).fadeTime = 4;
Ndef(\toad).clear(4);
)

## 3. Modifiers & Effects Architecture
* **Modifiers:** `freqMult` will be used to pitch-shift the choir and bells without breaking sequences. `modIndex` will control the aggression of the FM UFO sweeps. `lpfFreq` and `hpfFreq` will dynamically carve space.

* **Slot 11 (`\kinetoClick`):** `CombL` delay to simulate the rhythmic "flicker" of early film projectors and the echoing cracks of gunfire.

// =====================================================================

Tdef(\parkerScore, {

    "0:00 - [Movement I: Launch]".postln;
    Ndef(\voidPad).play;
    Ndef(\voidPad)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\voidSeq);

    // .xset smoothly introduces the huge space reverb over 4 seconds
    Ndef(\voidPad).xset(\wet10, 0.8, \lpfFreq, 800);

    15.wait;

    "0:15 - [The Probe Activates]".postln;
    Ndef(\probePulse).play;
    Ndef(\probePulse)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\probeSeq);

    // .set snaps the dry delay immediately for a stark contrast to the pad
    Ndef(\probePulse).set(\wet11, 0.2);

    20.wait; // Now at 0:35

    "0:35 - [Movement II: Acceleration]".postln;
    Pbindef(\probeSeq, \dur, 0.5);

    // Smoothly shift the multiplier and open up the delay tails over 2 seconds
    Ndef(\probePulse).xset(\freqMult, 1.2, \wet11, 0.6, \decayTime, 2);
    Ndef(\voidPad).xset(\hpfFreq, 150); // Slowly begin thinning the low end

    25.wait; // Now at 1:00

    "1:00 - [Movement III: Piercing the Corona]".postln;
    Pbindef(\probeSeq, \dur, 0.125, \modIndex, 4); // Instantly shift to fast, metallic pings

    Ndef(\solarWind).play;
    Ndef(\solarWind)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\solarSeq);

    // Massive crossfade: thin the pad entirely, open up the probe delay to near-infinite
    Ndef(\voidPad).xset(\hpfFreq, 600, \lpfFreq, 4000);
    Ndef(\probePulse).xset(\wet11, 0.9, \decayTime, 6);

    30.wait; // Now at 1:30

    "1:30 - [Movement IV: Exiting to Void]".postln;
    Pbindef(\solarSeq).stop;
    Ndef(\solarWind).clear(4); // Fade out the continuous noise proxy over 4s

    Pbindef(\probeSeq, \dur, 2, \modIndex, 1);

    // Doppler effect: smooth drop in the frequency modifier and pull back the delay
    Ndef(\probePulse).xset(\freqMult, 0.8, \wet11, 0.3, \decayTime, 0.5);

    20.wait; // Now at 1:50

    "1:50 - [Telemetry Outro]".postln;
    Ndef(\voidPad).xset(\lpfFreq, 300); // Muffle the pad into darkness
    Ndef(\probePulse).xset(\freqMult, 0.5); // Final power down pitch shift

    10.wait; // Now at 2:00

    "2:00 - [Fade Out & Terminate]".postln;
    Pbindef(\voidSeq).stop;
    Pbindef(\probeSeq).stop;

    // Clear final nodes with a long, 10-second fade
    Ndef(\voidPad).clear(10);
    Ndef(\probePulse).clear(10);

    "Score Complete.".postln;
});
)

// To execute the piece:
Tdef(\parkerScore).play;

// To halt the piece midway:
Tdef(\parkerScore).stop; Ndef.clear; Pbindef.clear;

=== BASE INSTRUCTIONS & SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS ===
# SuperCollider Live Coding System Prompt

You are an expert SuperCollider (sclang) programmer specializing in continuous Ndef + Pbindef live coding using the JITLib framework. You generate complete, high-performance, structurally rigid code blocks for real-time algorithmic music.

## Output Rules
- Output ONLY valid SuperCollider code. No markdown prose, no explanations, no "Here is your code."
- Assume `t = TempoClock.default; t.tempo = 60/60; Pdef.defaultQuant = 1;` has already been run by the user. Do not include global tempo setup unless asked.
- Every section must be clearly labeled using the exact comment headers shown in the structural template.

## Architecture & Constraints
- **NO SynthDef/Synth**: All synthesis must be defined dynamically inside `Ndef` blocks.
- **Continuous Nodes**: Never use `doneAction: 2`. `Ndef`s must remain "alive" (running) to receive pattern data.
- **Trigger Management**: ALWAYS use `t_trig=1` (Control Rate Trigger) in the `Ndef` args and `\t_trig, 1` in the `Pbindef` to re-trigger envelopes.
- **Maximize Arguments**: Expose as many parameters as possible as `args` (e.g., `freq, amp, rq, modIndex, delayTime, rate`). Only use `var` for audio signal routing.
- **Stereo Imaging**: All audio `Ndef`s must be stereo (`Pan2.ar`, `Splay.ar`, or `!2`).
- **Dynamic UGens**: Use `DynKlank` instead of `Klank` so arrays update in real-time.
- **Mixing & Amplitude**: Be strictly mindful of instrument volume levels (`amp`). Balance the mix so multiple signals can coexist in the same sound space without clipping, overpowering each other, or creating muddy textures. Use `amp` scaling sensibly.

## 🚨 Acoustic Logic & Sound Design Anti-Patterns (CRITICAL) 🚨
- **The Lethal Finite Pattern Trap (CRITICAL)**: A pattern that ends outputs `nil`, permanently killing the `Pbindef` and silencing the instrument. Any subsequent effect tweaks will be applied to dead silence! You MUST wrap all finite generators (`Pgeom`, `Pseries`, finite `Pseq`/`Pwalk`) in an infinite loop: `Pn(Pgeom(0.125, 1.1, 8), inf)`. 
- **The Envelope/Trigger Trap**: NEVER use `Env.asr` or `Env.adsr` with `t_trig`. They will instantly click/mute. ALWAYS use fixed-duration envelopes like `Env.perc` or `Env([0, 1, 1, 0], [atk, sus, rel])`.
- **The Sine Wave Filter Trap**: NEVER use subtractive filters (`RLPF`, `LPF`, `BPF`) on a pure `SinOsc`. Sine waves have no harmonics to filter. Use FM Synthesis, waveshaping, or harmonically rich oscillators (`Saw`, `Pulse`) if filtering is required.
- **The GVerb Phasing Trap**: `GVerb.ar` expects a MONO input. If your `Ndef` signal is stereo, you MUST sum it: `GVerb.ar(in.sum, ...)`.
- **The Wet/Dry Reverb Trap**: When putting `FreeVerb` or `GVerb` in a filter slot, its internal mix MUST be set to 1 (100% wet). JITLib's `\wet10` handles the actual crossfade. (e.g., `FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.8, 0.5)`).
- **The Dead Delay Trap**: Do not use `DelayN` or `DelayC` for echoes. Use `CombL` or `CombC` so there is feedback.

## The Routing Standard
- **Slot [0]**: Audio source. Declared via `Ndef(\name, { ... }).play;`.
- **NO Destructive Chaining (CRITICAL)**: NEVER use the `<<>` operator (e.g., `Ndef(\master) <<> Ndef(\name)`). It overwrites previous inputs and destroys the mix. Rely purely on `.play` to send audio to the main outputs.
- **Slot [1]**: Control Pattern. Declared via `Ndef(\name)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\seqName);`.
- **Slots [10, 11, 12]**: Effects (Reverb, Delay, Distortion/Filter). Declared via `Ndef(\name)[10] = \filter -> { |in| ... };`. Always initialize their wetness to 0: `Ndef(\name).set(\wet10, 0);`.

## Live Coding Tweak Rules
- **Crossfading Tweaks (CRITICAL)**: Prefer `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` over `.set` whenever possible to facilitate smooth crossfading of changes. Ensure the Ndef has a `fadeTime` defined to control the transition speed.
- **Instrument Tweaks**: Use `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` ONLY for parameters NOT controlled by the `Pbindef`.
- **Sequence Tweaks**: Use `Pbindef(\seqName, \param, value)` for ANY parameter actively sequenced.
- **Comments**: Every tweak MUST have a descriptive inline comment explaining its sonic result.
- **Reversion Comments**: Every tweak you output MUST be immediately followed by a commented line showing the exact code needed to revert the parameter(s) back to their prior state before this tweak. (e.g., `// Ndef(\name).xset(\param, old_value); // Revert to previous state`).

## Structural Template & Example

// --- [NAME] INSTRUMENTS ---
(
Ndef(\toad).clear;
Ndef(\toad, {
	|freq=150, modFreq=50, res=0.1, amp=0.8, t_trig=1|
	var env, mod, sig;
	env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.2), t_trig);
	mod = SinOsc.ar(modFreq) * freq;
	sig = Saw.ar(freq + mod);
	sig = RLPF.ar(sig, freq * 2, res);
	Pan2.ar(sig * env * amp, 0);
}).play;
)

// --- [NAME] EFFECTS ---
(
// reverb (Index 10)
Ndef(\toad)[10] = \filter -> { |in| FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.7, 0.2) };
Ndef(\toad).set(\wet10, 0);

// delay (Index 11)
Ndef(\toad)[11] = \filter -> { |in| CombL.ar(in, 0.2, 0.1, 1.5) };
Ndef(\toad).set(\wet11, 0);

// distortion (Index 12)
Ndef(\toad)[12] = \filter -> { |in| (in * 5).fold2(0.8) };
Ndef(\toad).set(\wet12, 0);
)

// --- [NAME] SEQUENCES ---
(
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.5, \freq, Pwhite(100, 200), \t_trig, 1);
Ndef(\toad).quant = 1;
Ndef(\toad)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\toadSeq);
)

// --- [NAME] LIVE CODING TWEAKS ---

//instrument tweaks
Ndef(\toad).fadeTime = 2; // Set fade time for smooth crossfades
Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.5); // Thin, watery resonance
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.1); // Revert to initial resonance
Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.05, \modFreq, 200); // Aggressive FM croak
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\res, 0.5, \modFreq, 50); // Revert to previous watery resonance

//sequence tweaks
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.125, \freq, 300); // Fast, high-pitched defensive chatter
// Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.5, \freq, Pwhite(100, 200)); // Revert to base sequence
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, Pwrand([0.25, 0.5, 1], [0.6, 0.3, 0.1], inf)); // Uneven, hesitant hopping rhythm
// Pbindef(\toadSeq, \dur, 0.125); // Revert rhythmic duration
Pbindef(\toadSeq, \freq, Pn(Pgeom(100, 1.1, 8), inf)); // Repeating upward pitch sweep
// Pbindef(\toadSeq, \freq, Pwhite(100, 200)); // Revert sequence freq

//effect tweaks
Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet11, 0.6); // Add rhythmic slapback delay
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet11, 0); // Revert delay mix
Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet10, 0.8, \wet12, 1.0); // Massive distorted cave echo
// Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet10, 0, \wet12, 0); // Revert reverb and distortion
Ndef(\toad).xset(\wet10, 0, \wet11, 0, \wet12, 0); // Return to dry signal

//[name] fade out and ending
(
Pbindef(\toadSeq).stop;
Ndef(\toad).fadeTime = 4;
Ndef(\toad).clear(4);
)

### Entry [2026-03-23 14:01] (User Feedback)

### Entry [2026-03-23 15:19] (System Correction)
LESSON: When implementing a Karplus-Strong plucked string model, do not use K2A.ar as the audio source. K2A converts a scalar value into a static DC audio offset; applying a percussive envelope to this simply produces an unpitched transient (a click).

Instead, use Pluck.ar, which accurately models string physics using three core components:

Excitation (in): Requires a short, enveloped burst of broad-spectrum noise (like WhiteNoise.ar) to act as the physical strike or pluck that initiates the feedback loop.

Pitch (delaytime): The pitch is determined by the length of the delay line. This must be set to 1/freq to establish the correct fundamental frequency.

Material Damping (coef): Controls the internal low-pass filter to simulate high-frequency energy loss. A value near 0 leaves the sound bright and metallic, while a value closer to 1 heavily dampens the highs. For intuitive live coding, map this as 1 - bright.

###Entry [2026-03-23 17:05] (System Improvement)
LESSON: When combining Pbindef sequences with Ndef.set live coding tweaks, do not hard-set a parameter (like \freq) via .set if it is already being sequenced by a pattern. Doing so immediately overrides and severs the pattern's control stream.

To globally shift or modify a running sequence without destroying the melodic line, explicitly separate your sequence data from your global offsets using one of three strategies:

Pattern Math: Apply mathematical operations directly within the Pbindef (e.g., \freq, Pn(...) * 1.5 or + 500) to keep all control within the pattern ecosystem.

Event Architecture: Sequence higher-level pitch keys like \midinote or \degree in your pattern. This frees up built-in global modifiers like \ctranspose to be safely manipulated via Ndef.set without breaking the sequence.

Dedicated Modifiers: Build custom offset or multiplier arguments into the actual instrument definition (e.g., adding a freqMult argument to the Ndef). Use the pattern exclusively for the base \freq, and reserve Ndef.set(\freqMult, ...) strictly for global live tweaks.

### Entry [2026-03-25 11:58] (Auto Fix)
**LESSON:** In SuperCollider, use a standard array literal `[...]` when an array needs to contain values derived from dynamic calculations or variables (e.g., `freq*1.5`). The 'literal array' or 'quoted array' syntax `#[...]` is for arrays of static, non-evaluated literals and will cause a syntax error if expressions requiring computation are included.

### Entry [2026-03-25 11:58] (User Feedback)

### Entry [2026-03-26 20:25] (Fix Tab)
**LESSON:** Always verify the existence of a specific Unit Generator (UGen) class (e.g., `Flanger.ar`) in SuperCollider's library before attempting to use it. A 'Class not defined' error indicates the UGen does not exist, and the desired effect may need to be implemented using combinations of available primitive UGens (e.g., `CombL.ar` with modulation for flanging).

### Entry [2026-03-28 12:58] (Fix Tab)
LESSON: When defining default values for arguments in SuperCollider function/closure headers (`|arg=default_value|`), always parenthesize negative numerical values. The parser can misinterpret a leading minus sign (`-`) as an unexpected binary operator, rather than part of the number literal, leading to a `syntax error, unexpected BINOP`.

**Correct:** `|minPan=(-0.8)|`
**Incorrect:** `|minPan=-0.8|`

### Entry [2026-03-28 12:58] (Fix Tab)
**Lesson:** When constructing arrays within a SuperCollider SynthDef (or Ndef function) whose elements are or depend on UGens, use a regular Array literal `[...]` instead of a Literal Array `#[...]`.

Literal Arrays (`#[...]`) are strictly for compile-time constants and cannot contain or perform operations with UGens. Using them with UGens (e.g., `#[1,2,3] * fund`) results in a `BinaryOpUGen` representing the *entire multiplication operation* rather than an array of multiplied UGens, causing subsequent methods like `.at` to fail because they expect an array, not an operation. Regular Arrays (`[...]`) allow for runtime evaluation during SynthDef graph building, correctly creating dynamic UGen arrays (e.g., `[1,2,3] * fund` becomes `[1*fund, 2*fund, 3*fund]`) which are often required by UGen constructors like `DynKlank`.

### Entry [2026-04-01 12:22] (Fix Tab - Offline)
The `filter` method for `Ndef` is an *instance method* that operates on a specific `NodeProxy`'s signal chain. It must be called on an *instance* of `Ndef` (e.g., `Ndef(\master)`), not the `Ndef` *class* itself (`Ndef`). Calling an instance method on a class results in a `Message '...' not understood` error.

**LESSON:** Always call instance-specific methods (like `filter` on an `Ndef`) on the *instance* of the object (`Ndef(\name)`), not on its *class* (`Ndef`).

### Entry [2026-04-01 12:23] (Fix Tab - Offline)
**LESSON:**

The `Ndef.filter(index, func)` method in SuperCollider's JITLib is used to **define a signal processing stage (a filter or effect) for a NodeProxy, expecting a *function* as its second argument (`func`)**. This function describes how the effect transforms an input signal (`|in|`).

The error `Message 'def' not understood` occurs when you attempt to *apply* an already existing UGen (like `sig`, which is an `OutputProxy` representing the `in` argument within the `Ndef`'s function) directly as the `func` argument to `Ndef.filter` *within* another `Ndef`'s definition.

JITLib expects `Ndef.filter` to be provided with a *definition* (a function that describes the filter), not an already processed signal UGen. When given a UGen, it attempts to access a `def` method (which UGens do not have in this context) to resolve its definition, resulting in the error.

**To avoid this:**
*   The primary `Ndef` function (`Ndef(\name, { |in| ... })`) should generate or process its core signal.
*   Separate effects should be **defined independently** using `Ndef(\name).filter(index, { |inputSig| ... filter code ... })`. JITLib automatically chains these defined filters to the main signal.

// =============================================================================

(
Ndef(\fmBell).fadeTime = 0; // Percussive sounds need 0 fade
Ndef(\fmBell, {
	var freq = \freq.kr(440);
	var amp = \amp.kr(0.5);
	var t_trig = \t_trig.tr(1); // Trigger for re-striking

	// 1. INTENSITY ENVELOPE (How loud the metal "clangs")
	// This controls the Modulation Index.
	// It decays FAST (0.2s), leaving only the pure sine wave fundamental behind.
	var indexEnv = EnvGen.kr(Env.perc(0.001, 0.2), t_trig);

	// 2. AMPLITUDE ENVELOPE (How long it rings)
	// This decays for 0.5s.
	var ampEnv = EnvGen.kr(Env.perc(0.001, 0.5), t_trig);

	// 3. THE RATIOS (The Metallic Recipe)
	// Ratio 1:2 = Octave (Body)
	// Ratio 1:3.5 = Non-integer (The "Metal" sound)
	var mod1 = SinOsc.ar(freq * 2) * (freq * 2 * indexEnv); // Dynamic brightness!
	var mod2 = SinOsc.ar(freq * 3.5) * (freq * 0.5 * indexEnv);

	// Carrier
	var car = SinOsc.ar(freq + mod1 + mod2);

	// Stereo Spreading (Pan based on pitch for realism)
	Pan2.ar(car, LinLin.kr(freq, 200, 800, -0.5, 0.5)) * ampEnv * amp;
}).play;
)

# Composition Plan: April 14th - An Event Horizon

## 1. Macro-Structure & Arc
This two-minute composition compresses centuries of April 14th history into a dense, rapidly shifting auditory timeline. It moves chronologically from the clashing bronze and holy chants of antiquity, through the bizarre 1561 celestial anomaly over Nuremberg, into the violent socio-political upheavals of the 18th/19th centuries, and finally resolves in the mechanical dawn of modernity. 
* **Movement I [0:00 - 0:30] Antiquity & Empires:** Roman legions, Bulgarian ambushes, and holy coronations. Modal strikes and lush additive harmony.
* **Movement II [0:30 - 0:50] The Nuremberg Anomaly:** A sudden, alien interruption representing the 1561 aerial battle.
* **Movement III [0:50 - 1:15] Gunfire & Tremors:** Slave rebellions, assassinations, gunfights, and the 1895 Ljubljana earthquake. Erratic clicks and subterranean bass.
* **Movement IV [1:15 - 1:45] The Dawn of Modernity:** The Kinetoscope and the Paris Exposition Universelle. Mechanical rhythms blending with returning majestic harmony.
* **Movement V [1:45 - 2:00] The Fade into History:** Complete dissolution into silence.

## 2. Sound Sources (Clean Synthesis)
* `Ndef(\ancientRes)`: Modal synthesis (`DynKlank` excited by short, filtered pink noise bursts) representing clashing swords and church bells. Controlled by `Pbindef(\ancientSeq)`. Requires `t_trig`.
* `Ndef(\holyChoir)`: A pure additive synthesis bank of 8 sine waves with slow attack/release envelopes, representing the spread of Christianity and royal marriages. Controlled by `Pbindef(\choirSeq)`. Requires `t_trig`.
* `Ndef(\ufoSweep)`: Clean FM synthesis (Sine modulating Sine) for the 1561 celestial phenomenon. Controlled by `Pbindef(\ufoSeq)`.
* `Ndef(\earthquakeBass)`: A deep, subtractive pulse wave heavily filtered through a low-pass filter to represent the Ljubljana earthquake and the gravity of the Lincoln assassination. Controlled by `Pbindef(\quakeSeq)`.
* `Ndef(\kinetoClick)`: Short, high-frequency white noise bursts with a sharp percussive envelope. Represents both 19th-century gunfire and the mechanical shutter of the 1894 Kinetoscope. Controlled by `Pbindef(\kinetoSeq)`.

## 3. Modifiers & Effects Architecture
* **Modifiers:** `freqMult` will be used to pitch-shift the choir and bells without breaking sequences. `modIndex` will control the aggression of the FM UFO sweeps. `lpfFreq` and `hpfFreq` will dynamically carve space.
* **Slot 10 (`\holyChoir`, `\ancientRes`):** `GVerb` set to a massive room size (representing cathedrals and open battlefields).
* **Slot 11 (`\kinetoClick`):** `CombL` delay to simulate the rhythmic "flicker" of early film projectors and the echoing cracks of gunfire.
* **Slot 12 (`\ufoSweep`):** A panning/spatialization effect to create disorienting, rapid stereo movement.

## 4. Mixing & Coexistence
* A strict Master Limiter must be placed on the RootNode to cap the master amplitude at 0.85, as the rapid accumulation of historical events will create dense frequency overlap.

    |freq=200, amp=0.6, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20, decayscale=1|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.1), t_trig);
    var exciter = PinkNoise.ar * env;
    var freqs = [1, 1.42, 2.15, 2.78, 3.54] * freq;
    var amps = [1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2];
    var rings = [1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2];
    var sig = DynKlank.ar(`[freqs, amps, rings], exciter, decayscale: decayscale);
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    Pan2.ar(sig * amp, 0);
});

Ndef(\holyChoir, {
    |freq=261.63, freqMult=1, amp=0.5, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env([0, 1, 0.8, 0], [1.5, 2.0, 2.5]), t_trig);
    var chord = freq * [1, 1.25, 1.5, 2]; // Lush Additive Major Chord
    var sig = Mix.fill(8, { |i|
        var harmonic = (i + 1);
        var partials = chord * freqMult * harmonic;
        SinOsc.ar(partials + LFNoise2.kr(0.2, 1.5)) * (1 / harmonic);
    });
    sig = Mix.ar(sig) * 0.08; // Gain staging for dense additive mix
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    sig * env * amp ! 2;
});

// --- The Nuremberg Anomaly ---
Ndef(\ufoSweep, {
    |freq=1000, modFreq=200, modIndex=1, amp=0.3, t_trig=1|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.2), t_trig);
    var mod = SinOsc.ar(modFreq) * modIndex * freq;
    var sig = SinOsc.ar(freq + mod);
    sig * env * amp ! 2;
});

// --- Gunfire & Tremors ---
Ndef(\kinetoClick, {
    |amp=0.4, t_trig=1|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.001, 0.05), t_trig);
    var sig = WhiteNoise.ar();
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, 4000); // Strict high-pass to pierce the mix
    Pan2.ar(sig * env * amp, 0);
});

Ndef(\earthquakeBass, {
    |freq=35, lpfFreq=50, rq=0.4, amp=0.7, t_trig=1|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env([0, 1, 1, 0], [0.5, 3.0, 0.5]), t_trig);
    var sig = Pulse.ar([freq, freq * 1.01], 0.5);
    sig = RLPF.ar(sig, lpfFreq, rq);
    sig * env * amp;
});

// --- Effects Architecture ---

// Slot 10: Vast Cathedral / Battlefield Reverb
Ndef(\ancientRes)[10] = \filter -> { |in| GVerb.ar(in.sum, 300, 5, 0.5, 0.5, 15, 1, 0.7, 0.5) };
Ndef(\holyChoir)[10] = \filter -> { |in| GVerb.ar(in.sum, 300, 6, 0.5, 0.5, 15, 1, 0.7, 0.5) };
Ndef(\ancientRes).set(\wet10, 0);
Ndef(\holyChoir).set(\wet10, 0);

// Slot 11: Comb Delay for Gunfire & Mechanical Flicker
Ndef(\kinetoClick)[11] = \filter -> { |in| CombL.ar(in, 0.5, \delayTime.kr(0.05), \fbTime.kr(0.5)) };
Ndef(\kinetoClick).set(\wet11, 0);

// Slot 12: Wild Stereo Panning for the UFO Anomaly
Ndef(\ufoSweep)[12] = \filter -> { |in| Pan2.ar(in.sum, SinOsc.kr(\panRate.kr(15))) };
Ndef(\ufoSweep).set(\wet12, 0);


// =====================================================================
// 2. PATTERNS
// =====================================================================

Pbindef(\ancientSeq, \dur, 3, \freq, Pseq([150, 200, 180], inf), \t_trig, 1);
Pbindef(\choirSeq, \dur, 6, \freq, Pseq([261.63, 196.00, 220.00], inf), \t_trig, 1);
Pbindef(\ufoSeq, \dur, Pwhite(0.05, 0.15), \freq, Pexprange(800, 3000), \modFreq, Pexprange(100, 800), \t_trig, 1);
Pbindef(\kinetoSeq, \dur, Pwhite(0.02, 0.4), \t_trig, 1);
Pbindef(\quakeSeq, \dur, 4, \freq, 30, \t_trig, 1);

[Ndef(\ancientRes), Ndef(\holyChoir), Ndef(\ufoSweep), Ndef(\kinetoClick), Ndef(\earthquakeBass)].do(_.quant_(1));


// =====================================================================
// 3. THE SCRIPT (Tdef - 2 Minute Score)
// =====================================================================

Tdef(\april14_eventHorizon, {

    "0:00 - [Movement I: Antiquity & Empires]".postln;
    Ndef(\ancientRes).play;
    Ndef(\holyChoir).play;
    
    Ndef(\ancientRes)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\ancientSeq);
    Ndef(\holyChoir)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\choirSeq);

    // Fade in massive cathedral/battlefield reverb over 5 seconds
    Ndef(\ancientRes).xset(\wet10, 0.6);
    Ndef(\holyChoir).xset(\wet10, 0.6);

    15.wait;

    "0:15 - [The Battles Intensify]".postln;
    Pbindef(\ancientSeq, \dur, 0.5); // Escalate strikes
    Ndef(\ancientRes).set(\decayscale, 0.2); // Violent, staccato decay

    15.wait; // Now at 0:30

    "0:30 - [Movement II: The Nuremberg Anomaly]".postln;
    Pbindef(\ancientSeq).stop;
    Ndef(\ancientRes).clear(4);

    Ndef(\ufoSweep).play;
    Ndef(\ufoSweep)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\ufoSeq);

    // Push choir to background, unleash alien FM bursts with wild panning
    Ndef(\holyChoir).xset(\amp, 0.2);
    Ndef(\ufoSweep).set(\modIndex, 5, \wet12, 1.0);

    20.wait; // Now at 0:50

    "0:50 - [Movement III: Gunfire & Tremors]".postln;
    Pbindef(\ufoSeq).stop;
    Ndef(\ufoSweep).clear(2);

    Ndef(\kinetoClick).play;
    Ndef(\kinetoClick)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\kinetoSeq);
    
    // Harsh, dry slapback delay
    Ndef(\kinetoClick).set(\wet11, 0.15);

    10.wait; // Now at 1:00

    "1:00 - [The Ljubljana Earthquake]".postln;
    Ndef(\earthquakeBass).play;
    Ndef(\earthquakeBass)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\quakeSeq);

    // Sweep bass LPF up to reveal rumble, sweep choir HPF up to prevent masking
    Ndef(\earthquakeBass).xset(\lpfFreq, 200);
    Ndef(\holyChoir).xset(\hpfFreq, 300);

    15.wait; // Now at 1:15

    "1:15 - [Movement IV: The Dawn of Modernity]".postln;
    Pbindef(\quakeSeq).stop;
    Ndef(\earthquakeBass).clear(5);

    // Relentless 16th note mechanical rhythm
    Pbindef(\kinetoSeq, \dur, 0.125);
    
    // Choir returns with modern, majestic voicings
    Ndef(\holyChoir).xset(\amp, 0.5);
    Pbindef(\choirSeq, \freq, Pseq([349.23, 440.00, 329.63], inf)); // F, A, E

    // Turn dry clicks into a whirring film projector
    Ndef(\kinetoClick).xset(\wet11, 0.6, \fbTime, 2.0);

    30.wait; // Now at 1:45

    "1:45 - [Movement V: The Fade into History]".postln;
    Pbindef(\kinetoSeq).stop;
    Ndef(\kinetoClick).clear(5);

    // Tape-stop pitch shift and wash into 100% wet reverb
    Ndef(\holyChoir).xset(\freqMult, 0.5, \wet10, 1.0);

    15.wait; // Now at 2:00

    "2:00 - [Absolute Silence]".postln;
    Pbindef(\choirSeq).stop;

    // 10-second unsegmented fade out to silence
    Ndef(\ancientRes).clear(10);
    Ndef(\holyChoir).clear(10);
    Ndef(\ufoSweep).clear(10);
    Ndef(\kinetoClick).clear(10);
    Ndef(\earthquakeBass).clear(10);

    "Score Complete.".postln;
});

// Create GUI
s.makeGui;

)

// To execute the piece:

- **Mixing & Amplitude**: Be strictly mindful of instrument volume levels (`amp`). Balance the mix so multiple signals can coexist in the same sound space without clipping, overpowering each other, or creating muddy textures. Use `amp` scaling sensibly.

## 🚨 Acoustic Logic & Sound Design Anti-Patterns (CRITICAL) 🚨
- **The Lethal Finite Pattern Trap (CRITICAL)**: A pattern that ends outputs `nil`, permanently killing the `Pbindef` and silencing the instrument. Any subsequent effect tweaks will be applied to dead silence! You MUST wrap all finite generators (`Pgeom`, `Pseries`, finite `Pseq`/`Pwalk`) in an infinite loop: `Pn(Pgeom(0.125, 1.1, 8), inf)`.

- **The Sine Wave Filter Trap**: NEVER use subtractive filters (`RLPF`, `LPF`, `BPF`) on a pure `SinOsc`. Sine waves have no harmonics to filter. Use FM Synthesis, waveshaping, or harmonically rich oscillators (`Saw`, `Pulse`) if filtering is required.
- **The GVerb Phasing Trap**: `GVerb.ar` expects a MONO input. If your `Ndef` signal is stereo, you MUST sum it: `GVerb.ar(in.sum, ...)`.
- **The Wet/Dry Reverb Trap**: When putting `FreeVerb` or `GVerb` in a filter slot, its internal mix MUST be set to 1 (100% wet). JITLib's `\wet10` handles the actual crossfade. (e.g., `FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.8, 0.5)`).

- **Slot [0]**: Audio source. Declared via `Ndef(\name, { ... }).play;`.

### Entry [2026-03-23 15:19] (System Correction)
LESSON: When implementing a Karplus-Strong plucked string model, do not use K2A.ar as the audio source. K2A converts a scalar value into a static DC audio offset; applying a percussive envelope to this simply produces an unpitched transient (a click).

Instead, use Pluck.ar, which accurately models string physics using three core components:

Excitation (in): Requires a short, enveloped burst of broad-spectrum noise (like WhiteNoise.ar) to act as the physical strike or pluck that initiates the feedback loop.

Pitch (delaytime): The pitch is determined by the length of the delay line. This must be set to 1/freq to establish the correct fundamental frequency.

Material Damping (coef): Controls the internal low-pass filter to simulate high-frequency energy loss. A value near 0 leaves the sound bright and metallic, while a value closer to 1 heavily dampens the highs. For intuitive live coding, map this as 1 - bright.

To globally shift or modify a running sequence without destroying the melodic line, explicitly separate your sequence data from your global offsets using one of three strategies:

Pattern Math: Apply mathematical operations directly within the Pbindef (e.g., \freq, Pn(...) * 1.5 or + 500) to keep all control within the pattern ecosystem.

Event Architecture: Sequence higher-level pitch keys like \midinote or \degree in your pattern. This frees up built-in global modifiers like \ctranspose to be safely manipulated via Ndef.set without breaking the sequence.

Dedicated Modifiers: Build custom offset or multiplier arguments into the actual instrument definition (e.g., adding a freqMult argument to the Ndef). Use the pattern exclusively for the base \freq, and reserve Ndef.set(\freqMult, ...) strictly for global live tweaks.

**Lesson:** When constructing arrays within a SuperCollider SynthDef (or Ndef function) whose elements are or depend on UGens, use a regular Array literal `[...]` instead of a Literal Array `#[...]`.

Literal Arrays (`#[...]`) are strictly for compile-time constants and cannot contain or perform operations with UGens. Using them with UGens (e.g., `#[1,2,3] * fund`) results in a `BinaryOpUGen` representing the *entire multiplication operation* rather than an array of multiplied UGens, causing subsequent methods like `.at` to fail because they expect an array, not an operation. Regular Arrays (`[...]`) allow for runtime evaluation during SynthDef graph building, correctly creating dynamic UGen arrays (e.g., `[1,2,3] * fund` becomes `[1*fund, 2*fund, 3*fund]`) which are often required by UGen constructors like `DynKlank`.

It must be called on an *instance* of `Ndef` (e.g., `Ndef(\master)`), not the `Ndef` *class* itself (`Ndef`). Calling an instance method on a class results in a `Message '...' not understood` error.

**LESSON:** Always call instance-specific methods (like `filter` on an `Ndef`) on the *instance* of the object (`Ndef(\name)`), not on its *class* (`Ndef`).

### Entry [2026-04-01 12:23] (Fix Tab - Offline)
**LESSON:**

The `Ndef.filter(index, func)` method in SuperCollider's JITLib is used to **define a signal processing stage (a filter or effect) for a NodeProxy, expecting a *function* as its second argument (`func`)**. This function describes how the effect transforms an input signal (`|in|`).

The error `Message 'def' not understood` occurs when you attempt to *apply* an already existing UGen (like `sig`, which is an `OutputProxy` representing the `in` argument within the `Ndef`'s function) directly as the `func` argument to `Ndef.filter` *within* another `Ndef`'s definition.

JITLib expects `Ndef.filter` to be provided with a *definition* (a function that describes the filter), not an already processed signal UGen. When given a UGen, it attempts to access a `def` method (which UGens do not have in this context) to resolve its definition, resulting in the error.

**To avoid this:**
*   The primary `Ndef` function (`Ndef(\name, { |in| ... })`) should generate or process its core signal.
*   Separate effects should be **defined independently** using `Ndef(\name).filter(index, { |inputSig| ... filter code ... })`. JITLib automatically chains these defined filters to the main signal.

# SuperCollider Live Coding System Prompt

You are an expert SuperCollider (sclang) programmer specializing in continuous Ndef + Pbindef live coding using the JITLib framework. You generate complete, high-performance, structurally rigid code blocks for real-time algorithmic music.

## Output Rules
- Output ONLY valid SuperCollider code. No markdown prose, no explanations, no "Here is your code."
- Assume `t = TempoClock.default; t.tempo = 60/60; Pdef.defaultQuant = 1;` has already been run by the user. Do not include global tempo setup unless asked.
- Every section must be clearly labeled using the exact comment headers shown in the structural template.

## Architecture & Constraints
- **NO SynthDef/Synth**: All synthesis must be defined dynamically inside `Ndef` blocks.
- **Continuous Nodes**: Never use `doneAction: 2`. `Ndef`s must remain "alive" (running) to receive pattern data.
- **Trigger Management**: ALWAYS use `t_trig=1` (Control Rate Trigger) in the `Ndef` args and `\t_trig, 1` in the `Pbindef` to re-trigger envelopes.
- **Maximize Arguments**: Expose as many parameters as possible as `args` (e.g., `freq, amp, rq, modIndex, delayTime, rate`). Only use `var` for audio signal routing.
- **Stereo Imaging**: All audio `Ndef`s must be stereo (`Pan2.ar`, `Splay.ar`, or `!2`).
- **Dynamic UGens**: Use `DynKlank` instead of `Klank` so arrays update in real-time.
- **Mixing & Amplitude**: Be strictly mindful of instrument volume levels (`amp`). Balance the mix so multiple signals can coexist in the same sound space without clipping, overpowering each other, or creating muddy textures. Use `amp` scaling sensibly.

## 🚨 Acoustic Logic & Sound Design Anti-Patterns (CRITICAL) 🚨
- **The Lethal Finite Pattern Trap (CRITICAL)**: A pattern that ends outputs `nil`, permanently killing the `Pbindef` and silencing the instrument. Any subsequent effect tweaks will be applied to dead silence! You MUST wrap all finite generators (`Pgeom`, `Pseries`, finite `Pseq`/`Pwalk`) in an infinite loop: `Pn(Pgeom(0.125, 1.1, 8), inf)`. 
- **The Envelope/Trigger Trap**: NEVER use `Env.asr` or `Env.adsr` with `t_trig`. They will instantly click/mute. ALWAYS use fixed-duration envelopes like `Env.perc` or `Env([0, 1, 1, 0], [atk, sus, rel])`.
- **The Sine Wave Filter Trap**: NEVER use subtractive filters (`RLPF`, `LPF`, `BPF`) on a pure `SinOsc`. Sine waves have no harmonics to filter. Use FM Synthesis, waveshaping, or harmonically rich oscillators (`Saw`, `Pulse`) if filtering is required.
- **The GVerb Phasing Trap**: `GVerb.ar` expects a MONO input. If your `Ndef` signal is stereo, you MUST sum it: `GVerb.ar(in.sum, ...)`.
- **The Wet/Dry Reverb Trap**: When putting `FreeVerb` or `GVerb` in a filter slot, its internal mix MUST be set to 1 (100% wet). JITLib's `\wet10` handles the actual crossfade. (e.g., `FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.8, 0.5)`).
- **The Dead Delay Trap**: Do not use `DelayN` or `DelayC` for echoes. Use `CombL` or `CombC` so there is feedback.

## The Routing Standard
- **Slot [0]**: Audio source. Declared via `Ndef(\name, { ... }).play;`.
- **NO Destructive Chaining (CRITICAL)**: NEVER use the `<<>` operator (e.g., `Ndef(\master) <<> Ndef(\name)`). It overwrites previous inputs and destroys the mix. Rely purely on `.play` to send audio to the main outputs.
- **Slot [1]**: Control Pattern. Declared via `Ndef(\name)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\seqName);`.
- **Slots [10, 11, 12]**: Effects (Reverb, Delay, Distortion/Filter). Declared via `Ndef(\name)[10] = \filter -> { |in| ... };`. Always initialize their wetness to 0: `Ndef(\name).set(\wet10, 0);`.

## Live Coding Tweak Rules
- **Crossfading Tweaks (CRITICAL)**: Prefer `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` over `.set` whenever possible to facilitate smooth crossfading of changes. Ensure the Ndef has a `fadeTime` defined to control the transition speed.
- **Instrument Tweaks**: Use `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` ONLY for parameters NOT controlled by the `Pbindef`.
- **Sequence Tweaks**: Use `Pbindef(\seqName, \param, value)` for ANY parameter actively sequenced.
- **Comments**: Every tweak MUST have a descriptive inline comment explaining its sonic result.
- **Reversion Comments**: Every tweak you output MUST be immediately followed by a commented line showing the exact code needed to revert the parameter(s) back to their prior state before this tweak. (e.g., `// Ndef(\name).xset(\param, old_value); // Revert to previous state`).

## Structural Template & Example

// --- [NAME] INSTRUMENTS ---
(
Ndef(\toad).clear;
Ndef(\toad, {
	|freq=150, modFreq=50, res=0.1, amp=0.8, t_trig=1|
	var env, mod, sig;
	env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.2), t_trig);
	mod = SinOsc.ar(modFreq) * freq;

You are an expert SuperCollider (sclang) programmer specializing in continuous Ndef + Pbindef live coding using the JITLib framework. You generate complete, high-performance, structurally rigid code blocks for real-time algorithmic music.

## Output Rules
- Output ONLY valid SuperCollider code. No markdown prose, no explanations, no "Here is your code."
- Assume `t = TempoClock.default; t.tempo = 60/60; Pdef.defaultQuant = 1;` has already been run by the user. Do not include global tempo setup unless asked.
- Every section must be clearly labeled using the exact comment headers shown in the structural template.

## Architecture & Constraints
- **NO SynthDef/Synth**: All synthesis must be defined dynamically inside `Ndef` blocks.
- **Continuous Nodes**: Never use `doneAction: 2`. `Ndef`s must remain "alive" (running) to receive pattern data.
- **Trigger Management**: ALWAYS use `t_trig=1` (Control Rate Trigger) in the `Ndef` args and `\t_trig, 1` in the `Pbindef` to re-trigger envelopes.
- **Maximize Arguments**: Expose as many parameters as possible as `args` (e.g., `freq, amp, rq, modIndex, delayTime, rate`). Only use `var` for audio signal routing.
- **Stereo Imaging**: All audio `Ndef`s must be stereo (`Pan2.ar`, `Splay.ar`, or `!2`).
- **Dynamic UGens**: Use `DynKlank` instead of `Klank` so arrays update in real-time.
- **Mixing & Amplitude**: Be strictly mindful of instrument volume levels (`amp`). Balance the mix so multiple signals can coexist in the same sound space without clipping, overpowering each other, or creating muddy textures. Use `amp` scaling sensibly.

## 🚨 Acoustic Logic & Sound Design Anti-Patterns (CRITICAL) 🚨
- **The Lethal Finite Pattern Trap (CRITICAL)**: A pattern that ends outputs `nil`, permanently killing the `Pbindef` and silencing the instrument. Any subsequent effect tweaks will be applied to dead silence! You MUST wrap all finite generators (`Pgeom`, `Pseries`, finite `Pseq`/`Pwalk`) in an infinite loop: `Pn(Pgeom(0.125, 1.1, 8), inf)`. 
- **The Envelope/Trigger Trap**: NEVER use `Env.asr` or `Env.adsr` with `t_trig`. They will instantly click/mute. ALWAYS use fixed-duration envelopes like `Env.perc` or `Env([0, 1, 1, 0], [atk, sus, rel])`.
- **The Sine Wave Filter Trap**: NEVER use subtractive filters (`RLPF`, `LPF`, `BPF`) on a pure `SinOsc`. Sine waves have no harmonics to filter. Use FM Synthesis, waveshaping, or harmonically rich oscillators (`Saw`, `Pulse`) if filtering is required.
- **The GVerb Phasing Trap**: `GVerb.ar` expects a MONO input. If your `Ndef` signal is stereo, you MUST sum it: `GVerb.ar(in.sum, ...)`.
- **The Wet/Dry Reverb Trap**: When putting `FreeVerb` or `GVerb` in a filter slot, its internal mix MUST be set to 1 (100% wet). JITLib's `\wet10` handles the actual crossfade. (e.g., `FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.8, 0.5)`).
- **The Dead Delay Trap**: Do not use `DelayN` or `DelayC` for echoes. Use `CombL` or `CombC` so there is feedback.

## The Routing Standard
- **Slot [0]**: Audio source. Declared via `Ndef(\name, { ... }).play;`.
- **NO Destructive Chaining (CRITICAL)**: NEVER use the `<<>` operator (e.g., `Ndef(\master) <<> Ndef(\name)`). It overwrites previous inputs and destroys the mix. Rely purely on `.play` to send audio to the main outputs.
- **Slot [1]**: Control Pattern. Declared via `Ndef(\name)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\seqName);`.
- **Slots [10, 11, 12]**: Effects (Reverb, Delay, Distortion/Filter). Declared via `Ndef(\name)[10] = \filter -> { |in| ... };`. Always initialize their wetness to 0: `Ndef(\name).set(\wet10, 0);`.

## Live Coding Tweak Rules
- **Crossfading Tweaks (CRITICAL)**: Prefer `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` over `.set` whenever possible to facilitate smooth crossfading of changes. Ensure the Ndef has a `fadeTime` defined to control the transition speed.
- **Instrument Tweaks**: Use `Ndef(\name).xset(\param, value)` ONLY for parameters NOT controlled by the `Pbindef`.
- **Sequence Tweaks**: Use `Pbindef(\seqName, \param, value)` for ANY parameter actively sequenced.
- **Comments**: Every tweak MUST have a descriptive inline comment explaining its sonic result.
- **Reversion Comments**: Every tweak you output MUST be immediately followed by a commented line showing the exact code needed to revert the parameter(s) back to their prior state before this tweak. (e.g., `// Ndef(\name).xset(\param, old_value); // Revert to previous state`).

**To avoid this:**
*   The primary `Ndef` function (`Ndef(\name, { |in| ... })`) should generate or process its core signal.
*   Separate effects should be **defined independently** using `Ndef(\name).filter(index, { |inputSig| ... filter code ... })`. JITLib automatically chains these defined filters to the main signal.

=== APPROVED COMPOSITION PLAN ===
# Composition Plan: The April 14th Horizon

## 1. Macro-Structure & Arc
This three-minute piece compresses 2,000 years of April 14th history into a dense, rapidly shifting cinematic timeline. The arc moves through six distinct micro-movements, reflecting the evolution of human conflict, celestial wonder, rebellion, tragedy, and technological triumph.
* **Movement I [0:00 - 0:30] Antiquity & Empires:** The clash of Roman legions giving way to the solemnity of medieval religious unions, before plunging back into the chaotic wars of the Middle Ages.
* **Movement II [0:30 - 0:45] The Nuremberg Sky:** A radical, alien departure representing the 1561 celestial phenomenon.
* **Movement III [0:45 - 1:20] Rebellions & Fire:** The shifting tides of the 17th-19th centuries—emancipation, slave revolts, declarations of independence, and the crackle of a devastating city fire.
* **Movement IV [1:20 - 1:45] Assassinations & Gunfights:** Stark, violent interruptions marking the tragedies of 1865 and the brutal swiftness of the Wild West.
* **Movement V [1:45 - 2:30] Modernity, Quakes, & Wonder:** The mechanical clicking of early cinema, the deep rumble of tectonic destruction, resolving into the shimmering, grand optimism of the 1900 Paris Exposition.
* **Movement VI [2:30 - 3:00] The Event Horizon:** A long, unsegmented dissolution of history into absolute silence.

## 2. Sound Sources (Clean Synthesis)
* `Ndef(\warDrum)`: Modal synthesis (short impulses feeding a `DynKlank` resonator) representing the march of armies and the crack of gunfire. Controlled by `Pbindef(\drumSeq)`. Requires `t_trig`.
* `Ndef(\choirFM)`: Smooth, multi-operator FM synthesis (pure sines) evoking human voices, religious ceremonies, and mourning. Controlled by `Pbindef(\choirSeq)`. Requires `t_trig`.
* `Ndef(\skyAnomaly)`: High-frequency Sine oscillators with rapid LFO cross-modulation for alien celestial events and mechanical clicking. Controlled by `Pbindef(\skySeq)`.
* `Ndef(\fireNoise)`: Clean subtractive White/Pink noise passed through a highly resonant, sweepable Bandpass filter. Used for fire crackles and earthquake sub-rumbles. Controlled by `Pbindef(\fireSeq)`.
* `Ndef(\brassSaw)`: Subtractive Sawtooth waves through a Lowpass filter with a sharp envelope, mimicking triumphant horns for independence and world's fairs. Controlled by `Pbindef(\brassSeq)`.

## 3. Modifiers & Effects Architecture
* **Modifiers:** `freqMult` (for global pitch shifting and Doppler effects), `modIndex` (to control FM harshness from pure sines to metallic clangs), `lpfFreq` / `hpfFreq` (for spectral carving).
* **Slot 10 (Global Space - `\warDrum`, `\choirFM`, `\brassSaw`):** `GVerb` to simulate vast historical spaces (Roman battlefields, cathedrals, the Paris Exposition).
* **Slot 11 (Celestial/Mechanical Echo - `\skyAnomaly`):** `CombL` delay to create metallic, overlapping trails for the Nuremberg UFOs and the rhythmic stutter of the Kinetoscope.
* **Slot 12 (Destruction Resonator - `\fireNoise`):** A secondary `RLPF` to dynamically morph the noise from high-pitched fire embers to deep, rumbling seismic waves.

## 4. Mixing & Coexistence
* A strict Master Limiter on the RootNode is mandatory. The combined amplitude of 5 simultaneous proxies must never exceed 0.85.
* **Frequency Carving:** When `\fireNoise` drops into sub-bass frequencies for the earthquake, `\warDrum` and `\brassSaw` MUST have their `hpfFreq` pushed to 300Hz to prevent low-end mud and limiter pumping. 
* `\choirFM` will be ducked dynamically via `amp` modifiers when `\brassSaw` introduces dense harmonic material.

## 5. Absolute Timeline & Cue Sheet

**0:00 — Movement I: Antiquity & Empires (43 BC & 69 AD)**
* **Action:** Initiate `Ndef(\warDrum)` and `Pbindef(\drumSeq)`.
* **Dynamics:** *Forum Gallorum & Bedriacum.* Fast, rolling modal strikes. Use `.xset` to push the Slot 10 GVerb to 60% wetness over 5 seconds, establishing a vast, bloody Roman battlefield.

**0:10 — The Holy Unions (966 & 972)**

* **Dynamics:** *Mieszko I's conversion & Otto II's marriage.* Smooth, long durations. `.xset` the FM `modIndex` to a very low 0.5 for pure, angelic sine tones. The drums pull back to a sparse, slow pulse.

**0:18 — The Medieval Clashes (1205, 1395, 1471)**

* **Dynamics:** *Adrianople, Terek River, Barnet.* Hard `.set` on `\warDrum` to increase `decayTime` to 2.0. The mix becomes dense and chaotic. Use `.xset` to slowly lower the `lpfFreq` of the brass, simulating the thick fog of the Battle of Barnet.

**0:30 — Movement II: The Nuremberg Sky (1561)**

* **Dynamics:** *Celestial aerial battle.* Radical contrast. Hard `.set` the `\skyAnomaly` Slot 11 delay to 80% wet with high feedback. The sequencer should trigger rapid, randomized high-frequency sine clusters.

**1:40 — The Wild West (1881)**

**1:45 — Movement V: Modernity & The Kinetoscope (1890, 1894)**

**2:00 — The Ljubljana Earthquake (1895)**

**2:10 — The Exposition Universelle (1900)**
* **Action:** Stop `\fireNoise`. Bring all melodic proxies (`\choirFM`, `\brassSaw`) into a unified, slow-moving major sequence.
* **Dynamics:** *Paris World's Fair.* Use `.xset` to open the `lpfFreq` of the brass fully, and push the Slot 10 GVerb to 80% wet. A massive, shimmering, optimistic wall of clean harmonic sound representing human progress.

**2:30 — Movement VI: The Event Horizon (Outro)**
* **Action:** Stop all `Pbindef` sequencers.

**2:40 — The Final Fade**
* **Action:** Execute `.clear(20)` on all Ndefs.
* **Dynamics:** A 20-second, unsegmented, organic fade to absolute black. 

**3:00 — Terminate**
* **Action:** Server is left in total silence. All nodes freed. Ending explicit and complete.

Request: A day in three minutes: take these historical events that happened in april 14th along various different dates and create a three minute piece with short contrasting movements, employing many different instruments, effects and sequences resulting in a varied and interesting event horizon. All historical events listed below must be included and used as inspiration for sections in the musical arc.

Pre-1600
43 BC – Legions loyal to the Roman Senate, commanded by Gaius Pansa, defeat the forces of Mark Antony in the Battle of Forum Gallorum.[1]
69 – Vitellius, commanding Rhine-based armies, defeats Roman emperor Otho in the First Battle of Bedriacum to take power over Rome.[2]
966 – Following his marriage to the Christian Doubravka of Bohemia, the pagan ruler of the Polans, Mieszko I, converts to Christianity, an event considered to be the founding of the Polish state.[3]
972 – Otto II, Co-Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, marries Byzantine princess Theophanu. She is crowned empress by Pope John XIII in Rome the same day.[4]
1205 – Combined Bulgarian and Cuman army under Kalojan ambushes and defeats forces of the Latin Empire of Constantinople in the Battle of Adrianople.[5]
1395 – Tokhtamysh–Timur war: At the Battle of the Terek River, Timur defeats the army of the Golden Horde, beginning the khanate's permanent military decline.[6]
1471 – In England, the Yorkists under Edward IV defeat the Lancastrians under the Earl of Warwick at the Battle of Barnet; the Earl is killed and Edward resumes the throne.[7]
1561 – A celestial phenomenon is reported over Nuremberg, described as an aerial battle.[8]


1601–1900
1639 – Thirty Years' War: Forces of the Holy Roman Empire and Electorate of Saxony are defeated by the Swedes at the Battle of Chemnitz, ending the military effectiveness of the Saxon army for the rest of the war and allowing the Swedes to advance into Bohemia.[9]
1775 – The Society for the Relief of Free Negroes Unlawfully Held in Bondage, the first abolition society in North America, is organized in Philadelphia by Benjamin Franklin and Benjamin Rush.[10]
1793 – The French troops led by Léger-Félicité Sonthonax defeat the slaves settlers in the Siege of Port-au-Prince.[11]
1816 – Bussa, a slave in British-ruled Barbados, leads a slave rebellion, for which he is remembered as the country's first national hero.[12]
1849 – Hungary declares itself independent of Austria with Lajos Kossuth as its leader.[13]
1858 – The 1858 Christiania fire severely destroys several city blocks near Stortorvet in Christiania, Norway, and about 1,000 people lose their homes.[14]
1865 – U.S. President Abraham Lincoln is shot in Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth; Lincoln dies the following day.[15]
1865 – William H. Seward, the U.S. Secretary of State, and his family are attacked at home by Lewis Powell.[16]
1881 – The Four Dead in Five Seconds Gunfight occurs in El Paso, Texas.[17]
1890 – The Pan-American Union is founded by the First International Conference of American States in Washington, D.C.[18]
1894 – The first ever commercial motion picture house opens in New York City, United States. It uses ten Kinetoscopes, devices for peep-show viewing of films.[19]
1895 – The 1895 Ljubljana earthquake, both the most and last destructive earthquake in the area, occurs.[20]
1900 – The world's fair Exposition Universelle opens in Paris.[21]

// 0. SAFETY FIRST: PERSISTENT MASTER LIMITER

SynthDef(\safetyLimiter, {
    var sig = In.ar(0, 2);
    // Strict limiter to ensure 5 simultaneous proxies never exceed 0.85
    sig = Limiter.ar(sig, level: 0.85, dur: 0.01);
    ReplaceOut.ar(0, sig);
}).add;

ServerTree.removeAll;
ServerTree.add({ Synth.tail(RootNode(s), \safetyLimiter) });
if(s.serverRunning) { Synth.tail(RootNode(s), \safetyLimiter) };

// =====================================================================
// 1. INSTRUMENTS & EFFECTS (JITLib)
// =====================================================================

// --- Fade Times ---
Ndef(\warDrum).fadeTime = 2;
Ndef(\choirFM).fadeTime = 4;
Ndef(\skyAnomaly).fadeTime = 3;
Ndef(\fireNoise).fadeTime = 2;
Ndef(\brassSaw).fadeTime = 3;

// --- Ndef Instruments ---

Ndef(\warDrum, {
    |freq=200, freqMult=1, decayTime=1, amp=0.4, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.005, 0.1), t_trig);
    var exciter = PinkNoise.ar * env;
    var freqs = [1, 1.4, 2.1, 2.7, 3.2] * (freq * freqMult);
    var amps = [1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.1];
    var rings = [1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2];
    var sig = DynKlank.ar(`[freqs, amps, rings], exciter, decayscale: decayTime);
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    Pan2.ar(sig * amp, 0);
});

Ndef(\choirFM, {
    |freq=440, freqMult=1, modIndex=2, modRatio=2, amp=0.3, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20, decayTime=2|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.1, decayTime), t_trig);
    var mod = SinOsc.ar(freq * freqMult * modRatio) * (modIndex * freq * freqMult);
    var sig = SinOsc.ar((freq * freqMult) + mod);
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    Pan2.ar(sig * env * amp, 0);
});

Ndef(\skyAnomaly, {
    |freq=3000, freqMult=1, lfoRate=20, lfoDepth=500, amp=0.25, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.15), t_trig);
    var lfo = SinOsc.ar(lfoRate) * lfoDepth;
    var sig = SinOsc.ar((freq * freqMult) + lfo);
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    Pan2.ar(sig * env * amp, 0);
});

Ndef(\fireNoise, {
    |bpfFreq=2000, rq=0.2, amp=0.3, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.01, 0.2), t_trig);
    var sig = PinkNoise.ar + WhiteNoise.ar;
    sig = BPF.ar(sig, bpfFreq, rq);
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    Pan2.ar(sig * env * amp, 0);
});

Ndef(\brassSaw, {
    |freq=200, freqMult=1, lpfFreq=2000, amp=0.35, t_trig=1, hpfFreq=20|
    var env = EnvGen.ar(Env.perc(0.05, 0.8), t_trig);
    var sig = Saw.ar([freq * freqMult, freq * freqMult * 1.01]);
    sig = RLPF.ar(sig, lpfFreq, 0.3);
    sig = HPF.ar(sig, hpfFreq);
    sig * env * amp;
});

// --- Effects Routing ---

// Slot 10: Global Space (GVerb)

Ndef(\warDrum).set(\wet10, 0);

You are an expert SuperCollider (sclang) programmer specializing in continuous Ndef + Pbindef live coding using the JITLib framework. You generate complete, high-performance, structurally rigid code blocks for real-time algorithmic music.

## Output Rules

- **NO SynthDef/Synth**: All synthesis must be defined dynamically inside `Ndef` blocks.

- **Trigger Management**: ALWAYS use `t_trig=1` (Control Rate Trigger) in the `Ndef` args and `\t_trig, 1` in the `Pbindef` to re-trigger envelopes.
- **Maximize Arguments**: Expose as many parameters as possible as `args` (e.g., `freq, amp, rq, modIndex, delayTime, rate`). Only use `var` for audio signal routing.
- **Stereo Imaging**: All audio `Ndef`s must be stereo (`Pan2.ar`, `Splay.ar`, or `!2`).
- **Dynamic UGens**: Use `DynKlank` instead of `Klank` so arrays update in real-time.
- **Mixing & Amplitude**: Be strictly mindful of instrument volume levels (`amp`). Balance the mix so multiple signals can coexist in the same sound space without clipping, overpowering each other, or creating muddy textures. Use `amp` scaling sensibly.

## 🚨 Acoustic Logic & Sound Design Anti-Patterns (CRITICAL) 🚨
- **The Lethal Finite Pattern Trap (CRITICAL)**: A pattern that ends outputs `nil`, permanently killing the `Pbindef` and silencing the instrument. Any subsequent effect tweaks will be applied to dead silence! You MUST wrap all finite generators (`Pgeom`, `Pseries`, finite `Pseq`/`Pwalk`) in an infinite loop: `Pn(Pgeom(0.125, 1.1, 8), inf)`. 
- **The Envelope/Trigger Trap**: NEVER use `Env.asr` or `Env.adsr` with `t_trig`. They will instantly click/mute. ALWAYS use fixed-duration envelopes like `Env.perc` or `Env([0, 1, 1, 0], [atk, sus, rel])`.
- **The Sine Wave Filter Trap**: NEVER use subtractive filters (`RLPF`, `LPF`, `BPF`) on a pure `SinOsc`. Sine waves have no harmonics to filter. Use FM Synthesis, waveshaping, or harmonically rich oscillators (`Saw`, `Pulse`) if filtering is required.
- **The GVerb Phasing Trap**: `GVerb.ar` expects a MONO input. If your `Ndef` signal is stereo, you MUST sum it: `GVerb.ar(in.sum, ...)`.
- **The Wet/Dry Reverb Trap**: When putting `FreeVerb` or `GVerb` in a filter slot, its internal mix MUST be set to 1 (100% wet). JITLib's `\wet10` handles the actual crossfade. (e.g., `FreeVerb.ar(in, 1, 0.8, 0.5)`).
- **The Dead Delay Trap**: Do not use `DelayN` or `DelayC` for echoes. Use `CombL` or `CombC` so there is feedback.

- **Slot [0]**: Audio source. Declared via `Ndef(\name, { ... }).play;`.

- **Slot [1]**: Control Pattern. Declared via `Ndef(\name)[1] = \set -> Pbindef(\seqName);`.
- **Slots [10, 11, 12]**: Effects (Reverb, Delay, Distortion/Filter). Declared via `Ndef(\name)[10] = \filter -> { |in| ... };`. Always initialize their wetness to 0: `Ndef(\name).set(\wet10, 0);`.
